## Failure Signature

- Test name: src/core/configStore.test.ts > Test-mode write guard (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR) — saveShipConfig/saveEnemyConfig/saveDifficultyCurves are registry-only under MODE=test
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
Test Files  1 failed | 381 passed (382)
Tests  4 failed | 8636 passed | 3 expected fail (8643)

 × saveShipConfig is registry-only under MODE=test: no fetch, no disk change
 × saveEnemyConfig is registry-only under MODE=test: no fetch, no disk change
 × saveEnemyConfig keeps Save As discoverable under MODE=test
 × saveDifficultyCurves is registry-only under MODE=test and keeps generation normalisation
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k 'src/core/configStore.test.ts > Test-mode write guard (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR) — saveShipConfig/saveEnemyConfig/saveDifficultyCurves are registry-only under MODE=test'` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

> Note (plan): the repository is a Vitest/TypeScript project, so the reproduction
> command must go through the test skill — `/skill:test` (changed or full scope).
> Direct `pytest`/`npx vitest` invocations are not permitted for agent runs.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/core/configStore.test.ts > Test-mode write guard (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR) — saveShipConfig/saveEnemyConfig/saveDifficultyCurves are registry-only under MODE=test` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — i.e. any `docs/` text describing the test-mode write guard or the registry-only save semantics is updated when the fix changes documented behaviour, and explicitly left unchanged (recorded in the completion comment) when behaviour is unchanged.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. The triage outcome is recorded on this item: either the confirmed root cause plus the fixing commit hash, or — when the failure does not reproduce on latest `dev` — the run reference and evidence that the four tests pass, with the item closed as not reproducible.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Prior context (planning survey)

The guard these tests cover shipped in AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR (commit `69e64725a`, "Test-mode write guard in configStore"). On latest `dev` the production code still contains the guard:

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isTestMode()` (= `import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'`) sits beside `isDev()`/`isSsr()`, and each of `saveShipConfig`, `saveEnemyConfig` and `saveDifficultyCurves` takes an early **registry-only** return after the `isDev()` gate (same registry mutation as the success path, no `putCsv`, no `reReadRegistry`).
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — `describe('Test-mode write guard (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR)')` holds six tests; the file's global `beforeEach` pins `MODE='development'` and each guard test opts back into `MODE='test'`.

The four reported failures are exactly the four guard tests that reach the test-mode short-circuit. The two tests in the same describe that return earlier (`DEV=false` unavailability) or deliberately do not use `MODE='test'` (the non-test dev control) were reported passing. That pattern points at the guard branch not being taken under the runner rather than at a broken assertion — but this is **not confirmed**: no test run was executed during planning (test-execution policy; runs go through `/skill:test`).

Candidate causes to check first (unconfirmed, rough order):

1. `vi.stubEnv('MODE', 'test')` no longer reaching `import.meta.env.MODE` in the classified project (a `define`/`env` change or setup-file interference), so `isTestMode()` is false and the save falls through to `putCsv`, where the `forbiddenFetch` stub throws.
2. Cross-test environment leakage in the integration project (`isolate`/`globalSetup`/`setupFiles` interaction, `vi.unstubAllEnvs` ordering) if the failure appears only in a full-suite run.
3. A concurrent dev-server write to the tracked CSVs (`src/data/*.csv`) invalidating the sha256 snapshot assertions — note the registry assertions in the same tests would still pass, so this alone cannot explain all four failures.

Related work:

- AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR — Feature: test-mode write guard in configStore (source of the guard and these tests; completed).
- AH-0MVS9UEHS009QH6J — Task: hermetic fetch handling for relative CSV calls in happy-dom (open; sibling under the same parent).
- AH-0MVS9TY0N0034LZT — suite-write regression guard (`src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts`), which also hash-snapshots the tracked CSVs.
- AH-0MVS9U6PP009JB0M — dev-server plugin root-containment guard.
- Parent: AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12.

Duplicate check: `wl search` / `wl list configStore` found no open item covering this failure. The only overlaps are the completed guard feature above (partial — it delivered the behaviour, this item asserts the tests pass now) and unrelated completed `[test-failure]` items.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` — the failing suite (`Test-mode write guard (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR)` describe).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isTestMode()` and the three registry-only save branches.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` — sibling suite that also pins `MODE`; check it stays green.
- `src/test/setup.ts` — integration project setup file (env/fetch interference).
- `src/test/trackedCsvGuard.globalSetup.ts` — suite-level tracked-CSV hash guard.
- `vitest.config.ts` — unit/integration/e2e project configuration.
- `vitest.projects.ts` — project classification, including this file's membership.

## Plan (no decomposition — effort XS, risk Low)

The pre-check (`plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`) returned `skip`: Extra Small / Low risk. This is a single-slice fix, so no child work items are created and vertical-slice phasing is a no-op at this size.

1. **Reproduce** — run the guard suite through `/skill:test` against latest `dev` and capture the real error text for the four failures (the triage evidence only lists test names).
2. **Diagnose** — confirm or eliminate the candidate causes above; record the confirmed root cause in a comment on this item.
3. **Fix** — smallest change at the correct layer: test-harness/env pinning if the guard never runs under the runner, or store code only if the guard is genuinely unreachable in test mode. Test-tooling only — no gameplay behaviour, so gym↔game parity is untouched.
4. **Verify** — changed-scope gate via `/skill:test`; the full suite must be green at the dev-push gate.
5. **Document** — update any `docs/` text describing test-mode save semantics if the fix changes documented behaviour (AC2); otherwise record that none was needed.
6. **Record** — completion comment with root cause and fix commit on this item, and a cross-reference comment on AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR.

If the four tests are green on latest `dev` and the failure cannot be reproduced, close the item with the run evidence instead of changing code (AC4).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this planning session. The effort/risk pre-check returned Extra Small / Low, the guard implementation (AH-0MVS9UAU8005SSQR) and its tests are present on `dev`, and the related items listed above gave sufficient intent for a single-slice fix. This run was a downtime dispatch with no interactive producer available.

- Q: none asked. Answer: n/a — no OPEN QUESTION entries; nothing was ambiguous enough to change the item's intent.

## Plan: changelog

- Plan skill (session herdr-1793449747-3202281-2377), 2026-10-31: pre-check `skip` (XS/Low). Added the planning survey (prior context, candidate causes, related work, duplicate check), a `**Key Files:**` section, the single-slice plan steps, a clarified AC2, new AC4 (triage outcome recorded), the Appendix and this changelog. data.description:
## Problem

The plan skill's autoplan pre-check is meant to decide whether an item needs planning from its effort/risk. On this epic (8 planned children, multi-week scope) the pre-check reported:

- `effort: "Extra Small"`, `risk: "Low"` → `decision: "skip"`.

The zeroed estimate was written by the plan helper's own estimator call, not derived from the item:

```python
# skill/plan/plan_helpers.py :: run_effort_and_risk
payload = json.dumps({
    "issue_id": target_id,
    "o": 0, "m": 0, "p": 0,
    "certainty": 100,
    "assumptions": ["Auto-generated by autoplan decision"],
    "unknowns": [],
})
```

`orchestrate_estimate.py` faithfully aggregates that zero payload, so every autoplan run stamps:

- `effort: XS`, `risk: Low`, PERT `O=M=P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided".

Evidence: comment `AH-C0MVXV4TGO0066OWH` on AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 ("T-shirt size: Extra Small … Recommended (with overheads): 0.00h"), and the follow-on `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment `AH-C0MVXV4TVH003G62N` ("Decision: proceed to implement (effort and risk below threshold)").

## Impact

- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` returns `skip` for **every** item, so the "small item" auto-skip path is indistinguishable from "the estimator wrote zeroes" — planning can be silently skipped for epics.
- The stored `effort`/`risk` fields are overwritten with false values, so the plan-approval gate (`Extra Large` + `High`/`Severe`) can never fire on real risk, and downstream scheduling reads a wrong estimate.
- Observed twice on this item: intake's autoplan pass and the plan session's pre-check both consumed the zeroed estimate.

## Expected behaviour

The autoplan estimate must not overwrite a work item's real effort/risk with a zero payload. Either:

1. derive the estimate from the item + its children (aggregate child WBS rows, count ACs/files), or
2. when no WBS/estimate inputs exist, leave `effort`/`risk` **unset** and return `decision: "error"`-equivalent "unknown" so the plan skill defaults to full planning (its documented conservative fallback), rather than writing `XS`/`Low`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` no longer posts `O=M=P=0` / `XS` / `Low` for an item that has children with non-trivial scope; a regression test covers an epic with children.
2. When the estimator has no real inputs, the work item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged and `plan-if-needed` falls back to full planning (or a documented `decision: "unknown"`), instead of `skip`.
3. A unit test asserts the pre-check returns `plan` for an epic whose children exist even if the estimator produces no numbers.
4. Existing plan_helpers tests still pass (full suite via the test skill).

## Key files

- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` — `run_effort_and_risk`, `make_autoplan_decision`, `plan_if_needed`
- `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` — aggregation / zero-payload handling
- `skill/plan/tests/` — autoplan decision tests

## Related

- discovered-from:AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 (observed while planning the optimisation pass).

---

## Plan (plan skill session, 2026-11-01)

**Implementation repo.** Every path in *Key files* above is relative to the
SorraAgents repo (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`); `skill/plan/` does not
exist in the AI_Hell checkout. The `AH-` item remains resolvable from SorraAgents
tooling through the shared prefix-to-sibling worklog scan
(`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py::_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`), so the fix can
be implemented in a SorraAgents worktree while tracking remains on this AI_Hell
work item.

**Reproduction observed during this session (2026-11-01T17:15Z).** Running the
pre-check against this very item reproduced the defect on itself:

- before the run the item's `effort` and `risk` fields were empty;
- `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed AH-0MVXVADEL005XNWM` returned
  `{"decision": "skip", "effort": "Extra Small", "risk": "Low"}`;
- the same run posted the zeroed `# Effort and Risk Report`
  (`O=0.00h, M=0.00h, P=0.00h`, "No detailed WBS items provided") and the
  `# Auto-Plan Decision` comment, and overwrote `effort`/`risk` with
  `Extra Small` / `Low`.

Those two bogus comments and fields are superseded by the genuine estimate posted
at the end of this planning session.

**Implementation sketch (test-first, one vertical slice).**

1. *Tests first* — `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py`:
   - epic-with-children case: an item with children and non-trivial scope must not
     yield `XS`/`Low`; `make_autoplan_decision` must not post the zeroed
     effort/risk report or the autoplan decision comment, and `plan-if-needed`
     must return `plan`.
   - no-real-inputs case: the item's existing `effort`/`risk` are left unchanged,
     no zero payload is written, and the decision is `plan` (never `skip`).
2. *Helper* — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`:
   - `run_effort_and_risk`: replace the hard-coded `o=m=p=0` / `certainty=100`
     payload with inputs derived from the item (children's stored effort/risk,
     child and AC counts), and return `None` instead of calling the orchestrator
     when no real inputs exist.
   - `make_autoplan_decision`: treat a `None` result as unknown → `do_plan=True`,
     write no `effort`/`risk`, and post no zeroed report/decision comment.
   - preserve `is_effort_risk_computed` idempotence: the unknown path must not
     write an `autoplan-decision-hash` comment, so a later run can still compute a
     genuine estimate.
3. *Defence in depth* — `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py`:
   only if needed, refuse or annotate an all-zero `o=m=p` payload rather than
   aggregating it into a confident `XS`/`Low`.
4. *Docs* — record the unknown-fallback in the plan skill pre-check section and in
   `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents).
5. *Verification* — run the `skill/plan/tests` scope through the test skill, then
   manually re-run `plan-if-needed` against an item with empty `effort`/`risk` and
   confirm it returns `plan` and leaves the fields unchanged.

**Vertical slice.** No phasing is needed: the test, helper and doc changes ship as
a single end-to-end slice. No child work items were created.

**Note on AC 2 (clarification, not a rewrite).** The existing plan-skill decision
vocabulary is `skip` / `plan` / `error`; introducing a fourth `unknown` value
would break callers such as the autoplan dispatcher. AC 2 is therefore read as:
the *behaviour* is "unknown → full planning", expressed as `decision: "plan"`,
optionally with an explanatory `reason`/log line — the zero-write behaviour is the
observable "unknown" signal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were asked in this session: the description's ACs and the
*Expected behaviour* section already resolve the issues that would otherwise have
needed an interview. The following are recorded as open questions/assumptions so
the implement session (and the Producer) can confirm them.

- **OPEN QUESTION (implementation repository) — directed to the Producer.** All
  *Key files* live in the SorraAgents repo, but this item is tracked in the
  AI_Hell worklog. *Assumption applied:* implement in a SorraAgents worktree and
  keep the work item here (prefix-to-sibling resolution makes `wl` work from
  either checkout). *Why it matters:* `implement.py start` selects the worktree
  from the repo it is invoked in, and `implement.py finish` refuses changes made
  outside that worktree — so the implement session must start in SorraAgents, not
  AI_Hell. *Alternative:* move/mirror this item into the SorraAgents worklog.
- **OPEN QUESTION (derive vs. unknown) — directed to the Producer.** AC 1 asks for
  no zero payload "for an item that has children with non-trivial scope"; AC 2
  allows an unset/unknown fallback. *Assumption applied:* derive from children's
  stored `effort`/`risk` when they exist, otherwise leave the fields unset and
  fall back to full planning. *Why it matters:* the derive path needs a defined
  aggregation rule (sum of child recommendations vs. max t-shirt vs. PERT).
  *Evidence:* `skill/effort-and-risk/scripts/orchestrate_estimate.py` aggregates
  `items`/`o`/`m`/`p`; child items currently carry no WBS rows, so in practice
  most runs will take the unknown path until estimates are propagated.
data.title: Autoplan effort/risk fallback stamps 0h / Extra Small / Low on an epic, silently skipping planning

# Assert the invariant where in-flight state is legitimate

Parent: AH-0MVX2DKC8001RRM4 (*Flaky unseeded PlayScene.test.ts integration assertions*).

**Goal (user story):** As a maintainer, the two flaky assertions should still fail on a real double phase advance or a genuinely lost spawn, while tolerating state that is legitimately in flight at the instant the test observes it — so a green run means the contract holds, not that the assertion was loosened.

## Context

- Failure A (`:2028`) asserts `boss.getPhaseNumber()` is exactly 2 after one `damageBossPhase(scene, boss)`. With a pinned seed and no live frame this is deterministic, so it can stay exact.
- Failure B (`:1107`) asserts `scene.getAliveCount() === wm.waveEnemyCount()` immediately after clearing a level. `getAliveCount()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5241`) counts spawned-and-alive entities, while `finishSpawnAnimations()` only completes the wormhole transit of entities **already released** — a later group still pending on the wave timer is not counted yet, which matches the observed 8-vs-9 shortfall. This may be a legitimate transient rather than a lost spawn.
- Precedent for the tolerance pattern: AH-0MURBER4L00821RR (`finishSpawnAnimations` seam) and AH-0MV5L6BVN005DP4I (hold-full mineral pause that can freeze `tick()`).

## Expected behaviour / outcomes

- Each of the two assertions has a **recorded decision** (exact vs invariant) with the reason and the evidence, so a later reader cannot mistake a deliberate tolerance for a weakened test.
- Where the exact count is legitimately unavailable at that instant, the test asserts the *invariant* — the wave's spawn window is fully released, or `aliveCount` equals `waveEnemyCount()` minus the groups still pending — with a comment naming the seam and this item.
- The assertions still catch the regressions they exist for: a double phase advance (phase skips 2) and a lost spawn (alive count never reaches the expected total even after the spawn window is released).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The decision for each of the two assertions is recorded on this item and reflected in an in-file comment: **failure A stays exact** (one hit pool advances the phase by exactly one, never two); **failure B** either stays exact (if the pinned seed makes it exact once the live frame is gone — demonstrated with a repeat-run result) or asserts the documented invariant.
2. If failure B is changed to an invariant, the new assertion still fails when a spawn is genuinely lost: it asserts the wave's full complement after the spawn window is fully released (e.g. draining the wave timer / calling the existing `finishSpawnAnimations()` seam until quiescent) and not merely "at least one enemy".
3. Every assertion touched by this child carries a comment explaining **why** it is exact or tolerant, referencing the seam (`getAliveCount` counts spawned-and-alive entities; `finishSpawnAnimations` only completes released entities) and this item.
4. No assertion is loosened without a recorded reason; exact counts remain exact wherever determinism makes them exact.
5. The verification for both `describe` blocks (playable-run and boss-encounter) is green through `/skill:test --scope changed`, recorded on this item.
- **Parent AC5 — Invariants where in-flight state is legitimate** (traceability restatement; covered by this item): **Invariants where in-flight state is legitimate:** any test that must tolerate in-flight bullets or spawn-animation lag asserts the invariant instead of an exact instantaneous count (e.g. phase index monotonicity, or alive count after the wave's spawn window is fully released), with a comment explaining why.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `:1107` (level-advance alive count), `:2028` (boss phase advance), plus the `killAllEnemies` / `finishTransition` / `finishSpawnAnimations` helpers those tests drive.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `getAliveCount()` `:5241`, boss phase/`damageBossPhase` path (read-only).
- `src/waves/` — wave timer and spawn-release accounting used by `waveEnemyCount()` (read-only).

## Constraints

- Test-only change; no production behaviour change.
- Do not weaken the assertions to "at least one" as a shortcut — the invariant must still catch a lost spawn (the parent's explicit constraint).
- Sanctioned channel only: `/skill:test --scope changed`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the shared helper child (2): the exactness decision can only be made once the boot is deterministic (no live frame, pinned seed).
